#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Accumulation experiment for GPT-2 XL with text-level mixing (nucleus sampling)
# Usage: bash run_accumulation_gpt2xl_nucleus.sh --mix_ratio 0.5 --cuda 0

MIX_RATIO=""
CUDA_DEVICE="0"
SEED=42

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        --mix_ratio) MIX_RATIO="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --cuda) CUDA_DEVICE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --seed) SEED="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown arg: $1"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

if [ -z "$MIX_RATIO" ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 --mix_ratio <0.5|0.25> [--cuda <0|1>] [--seed <42>]"
    exit 1
fi

export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$CUDA_DEVICE
export HF_HOME=/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache
export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com
export HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1

cd /root/autodl-tmp/recursive_gen_depth_est

echo "=== Accumulation GPT-2 XL Nucleus ==="
echo "  mix_ratio: $MIX_RATIO"
echo "  CUDA: $CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
echo "  seed: $SEED"
echo "  HF_ENDPOINT: $HF_ENDPOINT"
echo "  Start: $(date)"
echo ""

python3 scripts/accumulation_pipeline_gpt2xl.py \
    --mix_ratio $MIX_RATIO \
    --seed $SEED

echo ""
echo "=== Done: $(date) ==="
SHEOF
echo "Shell wrapper updated with HF env vars."

560 MB now. At this rate (~2 MB/s), it's going to take a while. GPT-2 XL model.safetensors is 6.28 GB = 6425 MB. 

Remaining: 6425 - 560 = 5865 MB / 2 MB/s ≈ 2933 seconds ≈ 49 minutes.

This is taking too long for me to poll. Let me instead submit the experiments and let them handle the download. HF transformers has proper file locking so concurrent downloads are safe. The experiments will just wait longer before starting training.


Actually, I can do better—I'll let the background download continue while submitting the experiments with a command that polls for a sentinel file before starting training.
